The first quarter of conference play was promising for the Razorbacks, with the only setback coming on the road against [[2019–20 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]], 79–77. Heading into a highly anticipated home game with [[2019–20 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|#10 Kentucky]], the Hogs were 14–2, with a 3–1 conference record. Arkansas led with less than nine minutes left in the game when Kentucky head coach [[John Calipari]] was ejected, sparking a Kentucky run and victory. From there the season bottomed out, with the Hogs finishing the last fourteen games of the conference season with a record of 4–10 for a final regular season record of 19–12 (7–11), including a five-game losing streak without star guard [[Isaiah Joe]] that featured back-to-back overtime losses for the first time in school history, in addition to a one-point loss.{{cite web |last1=Holt |first1=Bob |title=UA's NCAA goals begin with Vandy |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/mar/09/ua-s-ncaa-goals-begin-with-vandy-202003/ |website=wholehogsports.com |publisher=Arkansas Democrat Gazette, Inc. |accessdate=16 March 2020 |date=9 March 2020}} Heading into the last quarter of the conference season, Arkansas avenged earlier losses to [[2019–20 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] and [[2019–20 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], placing the Hogs back [[on the bubble]], but fell on the road to thirteenth-place [[2019–20 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], effectively knocking the Razorbacks out of tournament contention. After splitting the last two games of the season at home against LSU and on the road against [[2019–20 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], the Hogs were on the outside looking in, most likely needing to win the [[2020 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] to receive an [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] bid.{{cite web |last1=Gasaway |first1=John |title=NCAA tournament Bubble Watch: Updated look at the wildest bubble in years |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28577356/ncaa-tournament-bubble-watch-updated-look-wildest-bubble-years#SEC |website=espn.com |date=12 March 2020 |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=16 March 2020}} After winning their first-round game against [[2019–20 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] on March 11, 2020, the Hogs were slated for a rematch against [[2019–20 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] in the second round, but the SEC announced on March 12, 2020, that the SEC Tournament was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], with an announcement following from the NCAA later that day that the whole tournament was cancelled, along with all other winter and spring championships, ending the Razorbacks' season. The Razorbacks received some votes for the [[AP Poll]] throughout the non-conference season, but never earned a ranking, and stopped receiving votes by the end of January.{{cn|date=November 2025}} Mason Jones was voted the SEC Player of the Year by the league media, sharing the honor with [[Reggie Perry (basketball)|Reggie Perry]], a [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] player and former Arkansas commit, while the coaches' award went to [[Immanuel Quickley]], of Kentucky. Jones was the third Razorback to win the award, along with [[Bobby Portis]] and [[Corliss Williamson]]. Jones had an outstanding season, being named SEC Player of the Week four times, one of three SEC players to ever do so and the first in over a decade. Jones led the SEC in scoring, becoming the first Razorback to claim the SEC scoring title, while also finishing ranked eighth in the country for points per game. Jones led the NCAA in both free throw attempts and makes, while also having nine thirty-point games, the most by an SEC player in two decades. Jones broke [[Sidney Moncrief]]'s school record for free throws made in a season, in addition to being one of only three players in the previous thirty years to score forty points in a game multiple times in a season. Jones was named a consensus First-Team All-SEC player, the tenth time an Arkansas player has achieved that honor.{{cite web |last1=Cawood |first1=Mike |title=Jones Tabbed SEC Co-Player Of The Year; Consensus 1st Team |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/jones-tabbed-1st-team-all-sec-by-coaches/ |website=arkansasrazobacks.com |publisher=University of Arkansas |accessdate=16 March 2020 |date=10
